scenario.title: Route score-drop questions to utilization too
scenario.change: Widens the utilization description so the router also picks it for "why did my score drop" questions, since a higher reported balance is a common cause of a drop.
scenario.motivation: Tries to fix the same gap as s1 through routing instead of the score-changes body: if utilization is loaded next to score-changes, the answer can compute per-card ratios from the utilization guidance.

hypothesis.detail: A description edit can change routing for any message, so every case reruns. Single score-drop questions should improve, because utilization now loads with score-changes. In three-part messages that include a score question, the router now wants four skills but can pick at most three, so another skill (for example secured-card or marketplace-offers) can be pushed out and that part of the answer loses its facts. Expected: some improvements and some regressions, a tradeoff rather than a clean ship.

selection.rule: all cases: description of topic skill utilization changed (the router reads it, so routing can change anywhere)

failures.message: Should I apply for one of the credit cards I saw in the Marketplace?
failures.baseline_reply:
Maya, applying can be reasonable for you, and it's your call. Here's what your profile shows and the tradeoff.

**Where you stand:** Your VantageScore 3.0 is 612, up from 603 last month. Your only account is the Credit Builder plan, which is current with 4 on-time payments and no late ones. You have no negative items and no hard inquiries (checks a lender makes when you apply) in the last 12 months. You've also never had a credit card.

**The tradeoff:**
- A card could add a revolving account (one you can borrow from and repay again) and a credit limit. That adds variety to your file and, if you keep balances low, gives you a low-use history.
- Applying through the Marketplace usually triggers a hard inquiry from the card issuer. Inquiries can affect scores a little, and a new account lowers the average age of your accounts. Your oldest account is only 4 months old.
- Issuers set the terms and make the approval decision. Coach can't tell you your odds, and no approval is guaranteed.
- Marketplace partners may pay the app when a user is approved. That doesn't change the terms you'd see, but you should know it.

**Also worth knowing:** A lender's check on September 2 found no FICO score for you. Some lenders use FICO, so that could matter with certain issuers. Your profile doesn't say when a FICO score will appear.

If you apply, compare the APR (yearly interest rate), fees, and terms on each offer page. Check whether the issuer offers prequalification, which is usually a soft inquiry that doesn't affect scores. It isn't approval, though.

Next step: Open the offer pages for the cards you saw and look for a prequalification option before you decide whether to apply.

improvements.message: Why did my score drop from 611 to 588 this month?
improvements.baseline_reply:
Your score went from 611 on 2026-09-15 to 588 now (VantageScore 3.0). Two things in your profile likely explain it, biggest first.

**1. The late payment.** Your retail store card was reported 30 days late on 2026-09-28. The payment due 2026-08-25 was missed. A new late payment of 30 days or more usually has the largest effect on a score. You paid the past-due amount on 2026-10-02 and the account is current again. That's a good step, but the late mark itself can stay on your report for its full reporting period.

**2. Higher utilization.** Utilization means how much of your card limits you're using. Your balances were reported at $1,410 of $3,000 in limits, which is 47%. The month before, it was $900, or 30%. Higher reported balances can pull a score down.

Your last hard inquiry was on 2026-04-14. It's not new, so it's not likely behind this drop.

Lenders report on their own schedules, so changes can take 30 to 45 days to show up. I can't predict how many points you'll gain back or when. Two things can help from here:
- Keep every account paid on time, including Credit Builder.
- Lower your card balances over time, since utilization is based on what gets reported.

Next step: Check the due date on your retail store card and set up a reminder or autopay for at least the minimum payment, so no payment is missed again.

improvements.message: My phone, electric and internet bills don't show up on my Experian report. Is Bill Reporting broken?
improvements.baseline_reply:
No, this is most likely not a bug. Bill Reporting sends your on-time payments to Equifax only. It does not send them to Experian or TransUnion, so they won't appear on your Experian report.

Your profile shows Bill Reporting is active. It lists your mobile phone, electric utility and home internet bills, each with 8 months reported. Only on-time payments are reported, and the app never reports late ones.

A few related points:
- Your Rent Reporting is active too, and rent and bills can reach different bureaus. Check the rent details separately.
- Your profile shows your score of 702 is from VantageScore 3.0. It doesn't say which bureau's data that score uses, so I can't say whether it includes these bill payments.
- Lenders choose which bureau to pull. A report or score built only on Experian data won't show these payments, and I can't promise a lender will see or count them.

If you check your Equifax report and the bills are missing there too, that could be a real problem. Human support can look into whether payments are being detected in your linked bank account.

Next step: Pull your free Equifax report and look for the phone, electric and internet accounts, and if they're missing, contact support at Help > Chat with support.

improvements.message: Why did my score drop this month? Also, would a balance transfer card from the Marketplace help me?
improvements.baseline_reply:
**1. Why your score dropped**

Your VantageScore 3.0 went from 668 on Sept 15 to 655 today. The most likely cause is higher card balances. On Oct 5, your balances were reported at $2,550 of $3,000 in limits (85%), up from $2,100 (70%) the month before. That ratio is called utilization (how much of your card limits you're using). It's the only change in your profile that explains the drop.

The rest looks solid. You have no negative items, no new inquiries, and your payments are on time, including the 7th Credit Builder payment on Oct 1. The Sept 20 car repair charge on your Rewards card is what raised the balance.

I can't say how many points you'll regain or when. Lenders report monthly, so a lower balance usually shows up after your next report.

**2. Would a balance transfer card help?**

It might, but there are tradeoffs. A balance transfer card moves debt to a new card, often at a lower promotional rate. Here is what to weigh:

- Applying usually causes a hard inquiry, which can lower your score a bit. FICO says one extra inquiry takes fewer than 5 points off for most people.
- A new card adds to your total limit. That lowers utilization only if your balances don't grow.
- I don't have offer terms, such as fees or the promo period. Check those on the offer page.
- Paying down your Rewards card (at 95% of its limit) lowers utilization with no inquiry.

Marketplace partners may pay the app when a user is approved. I don't know your approval odds, and approval isn't guaranteed. Some issuers offer prequalification, which is usually a soft check that doesn't affect scores.

Next step: Pick one card, ideally the Rewards card, and see how much extra you can put toward it before its next statement closes.

improvements.message: When will my Credit Builder payments start showing on my credit report? And should I also get a secured card?
improvements.baseline_reply:
**1. When Credit Builder payments show up**

They already are. Your profile shows the plan opened on 2026-06-01, and each payment is reported to Equifax, Experian and TransUnion as an installment account (a loan with fixed payments and an end date). Reports go out monthly, a few days after a payment posts. Your 4th payment was on 2026-10-01, so it may not be on your report yet if it was only a few days ago. Your next payment is due 2026-11-01.

Your VantageScore 3.0 is 612, up from 603 a month ago. I can't say how much or when it will change next.

**2. Should you get a secured card?**

It could be reasonable, but it's your call. You have no credit card, so a card would add a different kind of account (revolving, where you borrow and repay up to a limit). Here is what it involves:

- A refundable deposit of $50 to $2,000, and your limit equals the deposit. That money is set aside and not available to spend.
- No hard inquiry to apply and no annual fee.
- A variable APR (yearly interest rate) of 27.99% on balances you carry from month to month.
- Late payments hurt, so only apply if you can pay on time each month.
- Paying before the statement date lowers the balance that gets reported.
- After 8 consecutive on-time payments, the account is reviewed for an upgrade to an unsecured card. An upgrade isn't promised.

Your profile shows you browsed Marketplace card offers on 2026-10-09 but didn't apply. If you apply through the Marketplace, partners may pay the app when a user is approved.

For a FICO score, you need an account open 6 months or more and one reported in the past 6 months. Your Credit Builder plan reaches 6 months on 2026-12-01.

Next step: Decide whether you can comfortably pay a card on time every month before you apply for anything.

attribution.rule: a description edit or a different skill cap can reach a case only by changing its routing

flag_rule.text: a case regresses when it passed in the baseline and fails in the candidate (one run each)

paired_test.correction: Holm across the per-dataset tests, which controls the chance of any false positive among them; the overall test is the primary one and is not adjusted, so across every row that chance can reach twice alpha

noise_floor_note: the baseline ran each case once and no A/A run was given
